For a complex potential $W(z)=\phi+i\psi$, the **streamlines** are the curves $\psi=\text{const}$ and the **equipotential lines** are the curves $\phi=\text{const}$. When $W$ is analytic, these two families are orthogonal. I write $z=x+iy$ throughout.

---

## (a) $W(z)=z^{2}+2z$

$$z^{2}+2z=(x^{2}-y^{2}+2x)+i(2xy+2y),$$
so
$$\phi=x^{2}-y^{2}+2x=(x+1)^{2}-y^{2}-1,\qquad \psi=2y(x+1).$$

**Equipotential lines** $\phi=C$:  $(x+1)^{2}-y^{2}=C+1$ — rectangular hyperbolas centred at $(-1,0)$ with asymptotes $y=\pm(x+1)$. The pair $C=-1$ gives the degenerate case $(x+1)^{2}-y^{2}=0$, i.e. the two asymptote lines themselves.

**Streamlines** $\psi=C$:  $y(x+1)=C/2$ — rectangular hyperbolas with asymptotes $x=-1$ (vertical) and $y=0$ (horizontal). The degenerate case $C=0$ gives the two straight streamlines $y=0$ and $x=-1$.

**Stagnation point:** $\dfrac{dW}{dz}=2z+2=0\Rightarrow z=-1$, i.e. $(-1,0)$. The two degenerate streamlines $y=0$ and $x=-1$ cross there at right angles, dividing the plane into four quadrants; in each quadrant the streamlines are hyperbolas. This is the classic **stagnation-point (90°-corner) flow** centred at $(-1,0)$. Since $W$ is analytic, the two hyperbolic families are mutually orthogonal.

---

## (b) $W=\bar z^{\,2}$

Here $\bar z=x-iy$, so
$$\bar z^{\,2}=(x-iy)^{2}=x^{2}-y^{2}-2ixy,$$
giving
$$\phi=x^{2}-y^{2},\qquad \psi=-2xy.$$

**Equipotential lines** $\phi=C$:  $x^{2}-y^{2}=C$ — rectangular hyperbolas with asymptotes $y=\pm x$; $C=0$ gives the two lines $y=\pm x$.

**Streamlines** $\psi=C$:  $xy=C/(-2)=\text{const}$ — rectangular hyperbolas with the coordinate axes $x=0$ and $y=0$ as asymptotes; $C=0$ gives the axes themselves.

**Important remark.** $W=\bar z^{\,2}$ is **not analytic**, so the Cauchy–Riemann equations fail (indeed $\phi_x=2x$ but $\psi_y=-2x$). Consequently the streamlines $xy=\text{const}$ and the equipotentials $x^{2}-y^{2}=\text{const}$ are **not orthogonal**: their asymptote directions $y=\pm x$ and $y=0,\,x=0$ are rotated by $45°$, and one checks directly that the gradients $(\,-2y,2x\,)$ and $(2x,-2y)$ have dot product $-4xy-4xy\neq0$ in general. Thus this "potential" does **not** describe an irrotational, incompressible flow; it is included only to contrast the analytic and non-analytic cases. The sketch consists of two families of rectangular hyperbolas, one with asymptotes $y=\pm x$, the other with asymptotes the coordinate axes, the two families intersecting at $45°$ rather than orthogonally.

---

## (c) $W=e^{-z}$

$$e^{-z}=e^{-x}(\cos y-i\sin y)=e^{-x}\cos y-i\,e^{-x}\sin y,$$
so
$$\phi=e^{-x}\cos y,\qquad \psi=-e^{-x}\sin y.$$

**Streamlines** $\psi=C$, i.e. $e^{-x}\sin y=k$ (constant $k$):
- $k=0$: $\sin y=0$, giving the **horizontal lines** $y=n\pi$ ($n\in\mathbb Z$). These are the channel walls / separatrix streamlines.
- $k\neq0$: $\sin y=k\,e^{x}$. Since $|\sin y|\le1$, each streamline exists only for $x\le -\ln|k|$. As $x\to-\infty$, $e^{x}\to0$, so $\sin y\to0$ and the streamline **asymptotes to the nearest wall** $y=n\pi$. As $x$ increases toward $-\ln|k|$, $|\sin y|\to1$, so the streamline bends toward $y=\pi/2+n\pi$ (the centre of its strip) and terminates there. Thus within each strip $n\pi<y<(n+1)\pi$ the streamlines are curves that hug the walls far to the left and bend toward the mid-line $y=(n+\tfrac12)\pi$ as they approach their right-hand end point.

**Equipotential lines** $\phi=C$, i.e. $e^{-x}\cos y=C$:
- $C=0$: $\cos y=0$, giving the **horizontal lines** $y=\frac{\pi}{2}+n\pi$ — exactly the centrelines of the stream-stripes.
- $C\neq0$: $\cos y=C\,e^{x}$, confined to $x\le-\ln|C|$, asymptoting to $y=\frac{\pi}{2}+n\pi$ as $x\to-\infty$ and bending toward the walls $y=n\pi$ near their right-hand ends.

The velocity is $\dfrac{dW}{dz}=-e^{-z}$, so $u=-e^{-x}\cos y,\;v=-e^{-x}\sin y$. On the centreline $y=0$ the flow is uniform in the $-x$ direction with speed $e^{-x}$ (accelerating to the left). This is the flow in an infinite array of parallel channels (or a single channel $0<y<\pi$) with the fluid speeding up as it moves toward $-\infty$; $e^{-z}$ has an essential singularity at $+\infty$ which acts as the source feeding the channels. Since $W$ is analytic, streamlines and equipotentials are **orthogonal**.

---

## (d) $W=\cos z$

$$\cos z=\cos x\cosh y-i\sin x\sinh y,$$
so
$$\phi=\cos x\cosh y,\qquad \psi=-\sin x\sinh y.$$

**Stagnation points:** $\dfrac{dW}{dz}=-\sin z=0\Rightarrow z=n\pi$, i.e. the points $(n\pi,0)$ on the real axis.

**Streamlines** $\psi=C$, i.e. $\sin x\sinh y=k$:
- $k=0$: either $\sin x=0$ (the **vertical lines** $x=n\pi$) or $\sinh y=0$ (the **horizontal line** $y=0$). These form a grid of separatrix streamlines: the real axis together with the vertical walls $x=n\pi$. They meet orthogonally at the stagnation points $(n\pi,0)$.
- $k\neq0$: $\sinh y=k/\sin x$. Consider the cell $0<x<\pi$ where $\sin x>0$. For $k>0$ we have $y>0$; the curve is symmetric about $x=\pi/2$, reaches its **minimum** height $y=\operatorname{arsinh}k$ at $x=\pi/2$ (where $\sin x=1$), and **rises to $+\infty$** as $x\to0^{+}$ or $x\to\pi^{-}$ (since $\sin x\to0$ forces $\sinh y\to\infty$). Thus each streamline is a U-shaped (actually ∪-shaped) arc opening upward, hugging the walls $x=0,\pi$ at large height. For $k<0$ one obtains the mirror image below the $x$-axis. Near a stagnation point, $\sin x\approx x-n\pi$, $\sinh y\approx y$, so $xy\approx k$: the familiar rectangular-hyperbola corner-flow pattern.

**Equipotential lines** $\phi=C$, i.e. $\cos x\cosh y=C$:
- $C=0$: $\cos x=0$, giving the **vertical lines** $x=\frac{\pi}{2}+n\pi$ — the centrelines of the cells.
- $0<|C|\le1$: $\cosh y=C/\cos x$. In the half-cell $0<x<\pi/2$ (where $\cos x>0$), for $C>0$ the curve has $\cosh y\ge1$, so it exists for $\cos x\ge C$, i.e. $x\le\arccos C$; it is symmetric in $y$, meets the $x$-axis at $x=\arccos C$ (where $\cosh y=1$, $y=0$), and rises to $|y|\to\infty$ as $x\to0^{+}$. These are arch-shaped curves. For $C=1$ the "curve" degenerates to the single point $(0,0)$ (and its periodic copies). For $C<0$ one gets the corresponding curves in the half-cell $\pi/2<x<\pi$.

Since $\cos z$ is analytic, streamlines and equipotentials are **orthogonal**. The pattern is the classical **flow in a periodic array of cells** (equivalently, flow in a channel of width $\pi$ with walls at $x=0$ and $x=\pi$): fluid rises along the walls and turns over, with stagnation points at the midpoints of the walls. It is also the complex potential for **uniform flow past a flat plate** (the segment $-\pi/2\le x\le\pi/2$, $y=0$ being a streamline along which the velocity is horizontal), by a suitable Joukowski-type reinterpretation.

---

### Summary of the sketches

| Potential | Streamlines $\psi=\text{const}$ | Equipotentials $\phi=\text{const}$ | Character |
|---|---|---|---|
| $z^{2}+2z$ | $y(x+1)=\text{const}$, hyperbolas, asymptotes $x=-1,\;y=0$ | $(x+1)^{2}-y^{2}=\text{const}$, hyperbolas, asymptotes $y=\pm(x+1)$ | Stagnation-point flow at $(-1,0)$; orthogonal |
| $\bar z^{\,2}$ | $xy=\text{const}$, hyperbolas, asymptotes the axes | $x^{2}-y^{2}=\text{const}$, hyperbolas, asymptotes $y=\pm x$ | **Not** analytic; families meet at $45°$, not orthogonal |
| $e^{-z}$ | $e^{-x}\sin y=\text{const}$; walls $y=n\pi$, curves bending toward midlines | $e^{-x}\cos y=\text{const}$; midlines $y=\tfrac\pi2+n\pi$ | Channel flow, accelerating to $-\infty$; orthogonal |
| $\cos z$ | $\sin x\sinh y=\text{const}$; walls $x=n\pi$ and $y=0$, U-shaped cell curves | $\cos x\cosh y=\text{const}$; centrelines $x=\tfrac\pi2+n\pi$, arch-shaped curves | Periodic cellular / stagnation flow at $(n\pi,0)$; orthogonal |
